statement: The dead worktree C:\Projects\ocentra-enforcer\.claude\worktrees\agent-a095dbb00dd5d53e0 held a near-complete, well-documented X06.P2 implementation (analysis/trace.rs, traces.rs, an impact.rs risk-classification extension, and tests/parity_trace_tools.rs + fixtures) that was directly usable after two corrections: (1) its analysis/mod.rs diff against current main accidentally dropped `pub mod clustering;` -- a real, still-used module (referenced from architecture.rs and clustering.rs itself exists on disk) -- which was almost ported over blind; only diffing against the CURRENT main-tree mod.rs (not assuming the salvage's diff was additive-only) caught this. (2) its impact.rs lacked a `detect_changes`-shaped response builder entirely (only the non-parity RiskFactors/ScopedImpactReport extension existed) -- the mission's explicit `detect_changes` hard-test requirement was not covered by the salvage at all and had to be authored fresh as `impact::detect_changes_view`/`DetectChangesView`/`ChangedSymbol`/`DetectChangesScope`.
why: Salvaging unverified prior-agent WIP requires diffing against the CURRENT tree, not trusting the salvage's own diff as authoritative -- a stale branch's diff can silently delete code that moved on without it.
howToApply: When salvaging from a dead/abandoned worktree, always run `diff` between the salvage file and the CURRENT main-tree version of the same file (not just copy it over), and grep the main tree for every symbol the diff appears to remove before accepting the removal.

statement: During this lane's work session, crates/enforcer-memory/Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, and Cargo.lock (workspace root) all contained literal unresolved git merge-conflict markers (<<<<<<< HEAD / ======= / >>>>>>> bbe14fc) that blocked `cargo build -p enforcer-memory` entirely for every lane touching the crate, not just this one. Separately, mid-session, the concurrently-running x06.8 federation lane landed untracked src/share.rs + src/federation.rs referencing an ed25519-dalek 2.2.0 API (`SigningKey::generate`) that does not exist in that version, and lib.rs briefly declared `pub mod redaction;` before src/redaction.rs existed on disk -- both transiently broke `cargo test -p enforcer-memory` compile for the whole crate (one shared test binary) for several minutes.
why: Multiple agents editing the same crate's shared entry-point files (Cargo.toml/lib.rs/Cargo.lock) concurrently, plus one lane landing files in a broken intermediate state, means a worker's own gate commands can fail for reasons entirely outside its own diff -- this is expected transient noise in a multi-agent build, not necessarily a regression to chase down and fix in a foreign file.
howToApply: Before concluding a gate failure is caused by your own changes, check `git status --short` on the failing file: if it is untracked or outside your claimed paths and another lane's mail/claims show it as their WIP, retry the gate after a short wait rather than editing someone else's in-flight file. Fix ONLY literal unresolved conflict markers in files you must touch to build at all (Cargo.toml/lib.rs/Cargo.lock), claim+release them immediately per the shared-file protocol, and mail the fix.
